cutoff_contract.note: 05:00 London is midnight in New York in both GMT and BST, so the session starts on the New York calendar day boundary and each eligible session is exactly 24 hours long

historical_validity.note: Structural validity is internal consistency plus the declared 05:00 London cutoff. Receipted validity additionally requires a full timestamp before the cutoff for every consumed input. The committed panel has no stamped print after the cutoff, so a genuine late-print rejection is not demonstrated by history; it remains untested rather than inferred.

parity.note: Reproduction of the stored calls only. These figures are not accuracy and not an edge claim.

cloud_bundle.note: The generated Cloud bundle reproduced the Node controller for both challengers over all 725 mornings.

performance.note: Gross directional replay, structural validation only, no costs, no slippage, no live execution and no multiple-testing or holdout claim. Test 1 is a broker proxy; tests 3 and 4 are blocked. Report this separately from reproduction and from the validation gate.

challenger.label: VIX level and risk regime
challenger.rule: VIX above 25 is safe-haven USD demand; below 16 is risk-on pressure

challenger.label: VIX 5-day change
challenger.rule: a 5-day VIX rise of more than one index point bids USD; a fall of the same size releases it

challenger.label: US 2-year yield 5-day change
challenger.rule: front-end yields up more than 5bp support USD; down more than 5bp oppose it

challenger.label: US 10-year real yield 5-day change
challenger.rule: real yields up more than 5bp support USD; down more than 5bp oppose it

challenger.label: Broad dollar 5-day momentum
challenger.rule: the dollar's own 5-day move continues: a rise above 0.15% is read as USD strength and a fall as weakness; FRED DTWEXBGS stands in for ICE DXY and is labelled as such everywhere

challenger.label: Gold 5-day change
challenger.rule: gold up more than 0.5% is a hedge bid against USD; down more than 0.5% is the reverse

challenger.label: NAS100 5-day change
challenger.rule: equities up more than 0.5% is risk-on and reads against USD; down more than 0.5% reads for it

challenger.label: EUR/USD 5-day change
challenger.rule: EUR/USD is USD inverted: a rise above 0.15% is read as USD weakness and a fall as USD strength; it stands in for the German 2-year leg the current model cannot reconstruct, and says so

challenger.label: USD/JPY 5-day change
challenger.rule: USD/JPY is USD direct: a rise above 0.15% is read as USD strength and a fall as weakness

limitations: n8n Cloud does not provide Execute Command, so the original host-command workflows cannot run there; the Cloud workflows bundle the controller instead.
The production-control adapter is not in the Cloud runtime; only the two frozen challengers are.
No committed morning has a stamped print after the 05:00 cutoff, so late-print rejection is untested on history.
The receipted gate refuses every one of the 725 committed mornings because most macro prints carry a date only.
The evidence covers four controlled dates, not a full n8n batch. The local controller remains the 725-morning batch path.
H1 is unscored and is not one of the two n8n children.
next_actions: Acquire a 05:00 receipt archive with full timestamps for the inputs the challengers consume, then rerun the receipted gate.
Record a late-print fixture separately and label it synthetic; do not add it to historical validity.
If the production-control adapter must run in n8n Cloud, package its replay dependencies explicitly instead of assuming filesystem access.
